mainTopic: Reward for מצוות: the scale of merits, whether reward comes in this world, and reward for resisting sin
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: the way רב planted his garden does not prove that he worried about כלאים outside ארץ ישראל. A new משנה then teaches that whoever does one מצוה receives good, long life, and a share in עולם הבא. The גמרא first raises a contradiction from משנה פאה. רב יהודה and רב שמעיה answer it by explaining how a person's merits and sins are weighed on a scale. A ברייתא then says the righteous suffer in this world while the wicked prosper. אביי answers that the righteous get both good days and bad days. רבא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יעקב, who holds there is no reward for מצוות in this world. רבי יעקב proves this from a son who did כיבוד אב ואם and שילוח הקן at the same moment, then fell and died, and the גמרא defends his proof against several challenges. רב יוסף adds that this understanding would have kept אחר from sinning, and the גמרא gives two versions of what made אחר go astray. Finally, רבא explains that 'sitting and not sinning' earns reward only when a person faces real temptation and holds back. The story of רבי חנינא בר פפי, which continues on the next amud, shows such a person.

steps.title: רב's garden proves nothing about mixed planting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting the proof from רב's garden. Planting four species on the sides and one in the middle would have shown concern for כלאים, but רב planted each species in its own bed for beauty or to make things easier for his attendant.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had planted four species on the four sides of the bed and one in the middle, that would be a fine proof. But here he did it for beauty. Or, it was to save his attendant trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an earlier discussion. It says the story about רב's garden does not prove that he was careful about כלאים outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One specific planting pattern, four species on the sides and one in the middle with space between them, would have shown that רב was keeping the species apart because of כלאים. Since he actually planted each kind in its own bed, there is another explanation. He did it for looks, or so his attendant could easily find each vegetable.
steps.whatToRemember: The story about רב's garden cannot be used as a proof. There are other good reasons for the way he planted.

phrases.english: Four species on the four sides of the garden bed
and one in the middle, that would work well.
But here, it was for the sake of beauty.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי נָמֵי מִשּׁוּם טִרְחָא דְּשַׁמָּעָא הִיא.
phrases.english: Or alternatively, it is because of the trouble of the attendant.
phrases.notes: This way the attendant would know exactly where each vegetable was when he was sent to get one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous section about רב's garden and כלאים outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רב's planting arrangement as proof that he worried about כלאים outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His planting can be explained by beauty or by convenience for his attendant, so it does not have to be about כלאים.

steps.title: The reward for doing one מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that whoever does one מצוה receives good, long life, and inherits the land. Whoever does not do one does not receive these things.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who does one מצוה is treated well, lives long, and inherits the land. Anyone who does not do one מצוה is not treated well, does not live long, and does not inherit the land.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It promises three rewards to someone who does one מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three rewards are good things, a long life, and 'inheriting the land,' which refers to עולם הבא. Read simply, the משנה sounds as if doing any single מצוה earns all of this. That simple reading is what the גמרא will question next.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Anyone who does one מצוה
is treated well, and his days are lengthened,
and he inherits the land.
phrases.notes: 'The land' here means עולם הבא, the World to Come.

phrases.english: And anyone who does not do one מצוה

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטִיבִין לוֹ, וְאֵין מַאֲרִיכִין לוֹ יָמָיו,
phrases.english: is not treated well, and his days are not lengthened,
and he does not inherit the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing one מצוה brings good, long life, and a share in עולם הבא. Not doing one brings none of these.

steps.title: A contradiction from משנה פאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes משנה פאה. It lists only a few special מצוות whose 'fruits' a person enjoys in this world, which seems to clash with our משנה's promise for any מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction. These are the things whose fruits a person eats in this world while the main reward stays for עולם הבא: honoring father and mother, acts of kindness, welcoming guests, and making peace between people. Torah study equals them all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה with another משנה. That משנה says only certain מצוות give reward in this world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only these special מצוות give reward in this world, then ordinary מצוות do not. So how can our משנה say that any single מצוה brings good things and long life? The two sources seem to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Their fruits (the reward in this world)

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'fruits' here is a picture. Think of money in the bank: the 'fruits' are the interest you enjoy now, and the 'principal' is the main reward saved for עולם הבא.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: The quote that follows is from פאה 1:1.

phrases.english: These are the things that a person
eats their fruits in this world
and the principal remains for him for the World to Come,
and these are they: honoring father and mother,
and acts of kindness, and welcoming guests,
and bringing peace between a person and his fellow,
and Torah study is equal to all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה from step 2 by quoting a conflicting משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's claim that any single מצוה brings reward.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משנה פאה limits reward in this world to a short list of special מצוות. That suggests ordinary מצוות do not bring such reward.

steps.title: רב יהודה: one מצוה that tips the scale
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that our משנה means one מצוה added to a person's merits that tips the balance in his favor. Such a person is treated as if he kept the whole Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: this is what the משנה means. Anyone who does one מצוה beyond his merits, so that the extra one tips his balance, is treated well and is like someone who keeps the entire Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the contradiction by reading our משנה in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה is not about any random מצוה. It is about the one extra מצוה that makes a person's merits outweigh his sins. Because that מצוה decides the balance, the person is rewarded as if he kept everything. So ordinary מצוות do bring reward, but only when they tip the scale.

keyTerms.meaning: In addition to his merits (tipping the balance)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what it is saying:
Anyone who does one מצוה
in addition to his merits is treated well,
and he is like one who keeps
the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 3 by reading step 2's משנה more narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה promises reward for any single מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה promises reward only for the one מצוה that tips a person's balance toward merit.

steps.title: Do the special מצוות reward even one alone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an implication from רב יהודה's answer. If ordinary מצוות reward only when they tip the scale, then the special מצוות in פאה would seem to reward even a single one, even when sins outweigh merits.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that for those special מצוות, even one by itself earns reward?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב יהודה's answer by asking what it implies about the special list in משנה פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If משנה פאה is different from our משנה, it must mean that those special מצוות give reward even when they do not tip the scale. That would be a surprising result. The גמרא asks whether that is really what it means.

phrases.english: By implication, those
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the special מצוות listed in משנה פאה.

phrases.english: even with one alone, also earn reward?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a surprising result from רב יהודה's answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רב יהודה's answer makes us read משנה פאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setting the פאה list apart suggests those מצוות reward a person even when his sins are more numerous, which is hard to accept.

steps.title: רב שמעיה: the special מצוות tip an even balance
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה explains that משנה פאה teaches something else. When a person's merits and sins are exactly equal, one of these special מצוות tips the scale in his favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה said: it comes to teach that if the scale was balanced, one of these מצוות tips it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה answers the question by explaining what is special about the מצוות in משנה פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The special מצוות do not reward a person whose sins outweigh his merits. Their special power is that when merits and sins are exactly even, one of them is enough to decide the balance for the good. So both משניות agree that reward depends on the balance of merits and sins.
steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה is about the one extra מצוה that makes merits outweigh sins (רב יהודה). The special מצוות in פאה are able to tip an exactly even balance (רב שמעיה).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that a person is judged by the overall balance of his merits and sins, and that one מצוה can make the difference.

phrases.english: Rav Shemaya said:
It comes to say that if it was evenly balanced,
it tips the scale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמַעְיָה: לוֹמַר שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה שְׁקוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 5 about the special מצוות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case that משנה פאה is speaking about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פאה מצוות reward a person even when his sins outweigh his merits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פאה מצוות decide the outcome only when merits and sins are exactly equal.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the righteous suffer and the wicked prosper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether someone whose merits outweigh his sins really gets good in this world. A ברייתא says the opposite: such a person gets bad, and someone whose sins outweigh his merits gets good.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that anyone with one extra מצוה beyond his sins gets good? But a ברייתא teaches: anyone whose merits are more than his sins gets bad, and he looks like someone who burned the whole Torah. And anyone whose sins are more than his merits gets good, and he looks like someone who kept the whole Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה's explanation of our משנה. It brings a ברייתא that seems to say the exact reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said that a person whose merits tip the scale gets good in this world. The ברייתא says that person gets suffering, and the one whose sins are greater gets good. The two sources clash head-on about who prospers in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction; a source is brought that clashes with what was just said
Bad is done to him; he is made to suffer

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mean the righteous person really burned the Torah. It means that, because of his suffering, he looks to other people as if he did.

phrases.english: And does anyone who does one מצוה
beyond his merits really have good done to him?
But they pointed out a contradiction:
Anyone whose merits are more than his sins
has bad done to him,

phrases.aramaic: וְדוֹמֶה כְּמִי שֶׁשָּׂרַף כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
phrases.english: and he looks like someone who burned the entire Torah

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שִׁיֵּיר מִמֶּנָּה אֲפִילּוּ אוֹת אַחַת.
phrases.english: and did not leave even one letter of it.
And anyone whose sins are more than his merits
has good done to him,

phrases.aramaic: וְדוֹמֶה כְּמִי שֶׁקִּיֵּים כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
phrases.english: and he looks like someone who kept the entire Torah
and did not leave out even one letter of it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב יהודה's reading of the משנה (Step 4) and challenges it with an outside ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's explanation that a person whose merits outweigh his sins receives good in this world.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction from a ברייתא: the person whose merits are greater suffers in this world, and the one whose sins are greater prospers.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה means a mix of good days and bad days
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that our משנה does not promise only good. The righteous person gets good days as reward and bad days that clean away his sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Our משנה means that he is given a good day and a bad day.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by showing that both sources can be true together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the משנה's "good" and the ברייתא's "bad" both happen to the same righteous person. He gets some good days as reward for his מצוות and some bad days to pay for his sins. So the sources do not really argue.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the one this גמרא is discussing

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Our mishna means that they give him
a good day and a bad day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַתְנִיתִין דְּעָבְדִין לֵיהּ יוֹם טָב וָיוֹם בִּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: both sources describe parts of the same experience.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to promise only good, and the ברייתא only bad, for the same person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The righteous person gets both: good days as reward and bad days to clean away his sins.

steps.title: רבא: the ברייתא follows רבי יעקב, who holds there is no reward in this world
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. The two sources really disagree, and the ברייתא follows רבי יעקב, who says a מצוה is not rewarded in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי יעקב, who said: There is no reward for a מצוה in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction differently. He says the ברייתא follows one תנא, רבי יעקב, while our משנה follows another view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי made the two sources agree, but רבא says they do not. The ברייתא matches רבי יעקב, who holds that all reward for מצוות comes in the next world. That is why the righteous person can suffer here.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? Used to tie a source to a specific Tanna
The reward for doing a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: The "this" (הא) in רבא's answer is the ברייתא, not our משנה. Our משנה, which promises good in this world, does not follow רבי יעקב.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yaakov's,
phrases.notes: "This" means the ברייתא from Step 7, the one where the righteous suffer.

phrases.english: who said: reward for a מצוה
does not exist in this world.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, competing answer to the contradiction of Step 7, instead of אביי's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the two sources follow different תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to give one shared view about reward in this world.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יעקב (no reward in this world), and our משנה follows a different view.

steps.title: רבי יעקב's rule: every promised reward depends on תחיית המתים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יעקב's statement that any reward written next to a מצוה is really given after תחיית המתים. It then brings the two פסוקים promising long life: כיבוד אב ואם and שילוח הקן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יעקב says, there is no מצוה in the Torah with its reward written next to it whose reward does not depend on תחיית המתים. By כיבוד אב ואם it says: "So that your days will be long and so that it will be good for you." By שילוח הקן it says: "So that it will be good for you and you will have long days."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבי יעקב says his view, backing up רבא's answer. It is also setting up the story that comes next by quoting the two long-life promises.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב says that when the Torah writes a reward next to a מצוה, that reward comes after תחיית המתים, not in this life. The two פסוקים he quotes promise goodness and long days. The next step will show why these promises cannot mean this world.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches; brings a Tannaic source as proof
Its reward is written right next to it in the Torah
The rising of the dead in the future
Sending away the mother bird before taking the young from the nest

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yaakov says:
There is not a single מצוה
written in the Torah
whose reward is written next to it
that does not depend on the resurrection of the dead.
phrases.notes: He means the reward is actually given after תחיית המתים, not in this life.

phrases.english: About honoring father and mother it is written:
"So that your days may be long
and so that it may go well with you,"
about sending away the mother bird from the nest it is written:
"So that it may go well with you and you may live long."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's claim in Step 9 by quoting רבי יעקב's own words.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי יעקב holds there is no reward for מצוות in this world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יעקב says every written reward depends on תחיית המתים, together with the long-life פסוקים of כיבוד אב ואם and שילוח הקן.

steps.title: The boy who did both long-life מצוות and died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב describes a boy who, at his father's request, sent away the mother bird and took the chicks, doing both long-life מצוות at once. On the way down he fell and died, so where was his long, good life?
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is a case where a father told his son: Climb up the building and bring me chicks. He climbed up, sent away the mother, and took the young. On the way back he fell and died. Where is this boy's good life, and where is his long life?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב gives a real case that seems to break the Torah's promise if it is read as this-world reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boy did exactly the two מצוות that promise long life, and he did them at the same time. Yet he died while doing them. So the promise of long, good days cannot be talking about this world.

phrases.english: Here is one whose father said to him:
Climb up the building and bring me chicks,
and he climbed up the building

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁלַּח אֶת הָאֵם וְנָטַל אֶת הַבָּנִים
phrases.english: and sent away the mother and took the young,
and on his way back he fell and died.
Where is this one's good life,
and where is this one's long life?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a real case to show that the פסוקים quoted in Step 10 cannot mean reward in this world.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יעקב's rule that written rewards are not paid in this world.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of the boy who died while doing both מצוות that promise long life.

steps.title: The promises refer to the world that is all good and all long
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב concludes that "so it will be good for you" means in the world that is completely good, and "so your days will be long" means in the world that is endlessly long.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: "So that it will be good for you" means in the world that is all good. "So that your days will be long" means in the world that is all long.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב gives his final reading of the פסוקים. The promised good and long life belong to עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the boy died, the promise cannot mean a long life here. So רבי יעקב reads it as reward in the next world, which is fully good and never ends. This completes the support for רבא's answer that the ברייתא follows רבי יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; brings in the correct reading after rejecting the first one
The world that is entirely good, the next world
The world that is entirely long, which never ends

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. אביי says the righteous get both good and bad days in this world. רבא says the ברייתא follows רבי יעקב, who holds that reward for מצוות comes only in עולם הבא, as the story of the boy who fell proves.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the idea that the true reward for מצוות is in עולם הבא. It also helps explain why righteous people can suffer in this world.

phrases.english: Rather: "So that it may go well with you"
means in the world that is entirely good,
and "so that your days may be long"
means in the world that is entirely long.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: ״לְמַעַן יִיטַב לָךְ״ – לְעוֹלָם שֶׁכּוּלּוֹ טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question "where is his long, good life?" from Step 11 by moving the promise to עולם הבא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The Torah's promises of goodness and long life for מצוות refer to עולם הבא. This is רבי יעקב's view, which the ברייתא follows according to רבא.

steps.title: Maybe the story never happened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יעקב's story of the boy is only an imagined case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it never happened this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יעקב's proof by asking whether the boy's death was ever a real event. Maybe it is only a made-up example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב's whole proof rests on the story. If it is only a 'what if,' you could argue that in real life everyone who does these מצוות does get long life in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: It did not happen this way

phrases.english: But perhaps it never happened this way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual basis of רבי יעקב's proof in steps 11-12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יעקב's story of the boy who died.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hypothetical case cannot prove what actually happens in this world.

steps.title: רבי יעקב saw it happen
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי יעקב was an eyewitness to such a case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב saw an actual event.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story is real. רבי יעקב saw it with his own eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the event really happened, the proof cannot be brushed aside as theory. The next challenges have to look for a different reason the boy died.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov saw an actual incident.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer: the event was witnessed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story might be only a made-up case.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a real event that רבי יעקב saw.

steps.title: Maybe he was thinking about a sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the boy died as punishment for sinful thoughts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he was thinking about a sin at the time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now accepts that the story happened, but offers another reason for the boy's death: maybe he was thinking about doing a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he was punished for bad thoughts, his death would not show that the מצוות went unrewarded. The punishment could have outweighed the reward.

phrases.english: But perhaps he was thinking about a sin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the factual objection fails, a new reason for the death is offered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the boy's death proves there is no reward in this world.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His death may have been punishment for sinful thoughts, not a lack of reward.

steps.title: Bad thoughts are not punished like actions
steps.stepSummary: The answer: הקדוש ברוך הוא does not count a bad thought as if it were a deed.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא does not join a bad thought to an action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a rule: a person is not punished for merely thinking about a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since thoughts of sin alone are not punished, they cannot explain the boy's death. The proof still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Joins it to an action (counts it as if done)

phrases.english: A bad thought,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not join it to an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies a general principle that removes the suggested cause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He died as punishment for thinking about a sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bad thoughts alone are not punished, so that cannot be why he died.

steps.title: Maybe he was thinking about עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests he was thinking about עבודה זרה, which is punished even as a thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he was thinking about idol worship, and it is written: "So I may take the house of Israel in their heart"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an exception to the last rule. Thoughts of עבודה זרה are punished, as a פסוק shows, so maybe that is why the boy died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of catching Israel 'in their heart,' meaning God holds people responsible for idolatrous thoughts. This reopens the possibility that the boy's death was a punishment.

phrases.english: But perhaps he was thinking about idol worship,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״לְמַעַן תְּפֹשׂ אֶת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּלִבָּם״?!
phrases.english: and it is written: "So that I may seize the house of Israel in their heart"?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds an exception to the rule of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that thoughts are not punished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Idolatrous thoughts are an exception and are punished, so the death could still be a punishment.

steps.title: Then why didn't the מצוות protect him?
steps.stepSummary: The answer: this is exactly רבי יעקב's point. If מצוות were rewarded here, they would have protected him from such thoughts.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is exactly what he is saying: if you think there is reward for a מצוה in this world, why didn't the מצוות protect him so that he would not come to such thoughts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the challenge into more support for רבי יעקב. If doing מצוות earned protection in this world, the boy should have been shielded from thinking about עבודה זרה in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either way the proof works. If he died with no sin, the מצוות did not save him; if he had idolatrous thoughts, the מצוות did not protect him from them. Both show that the reward is not given in this world.

phrases.english: He too is saying this:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יעקב. The question is already built into his proof.

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ שְׂכַר מִצְוָה בְּהַאי עָלְמָא,
phrases.english: If you think there is reward for a מצוה in this world,
why didn't the מצוות protect him

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לֵיתֵי לִידֵי הִרְהוּר?
phrases.english: so that he would not come to sinful thoughts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by showing the objection actually supports רבי יעקב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turns the objection into support for the original claim.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His idolatrous thoughts explain his death, so the proof fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: Real reward in this world would have protected him from those thoughts, so the proof stands either way.

steps.title: People on a מצוה mission are not harmed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story from רבי אלעזר's rule that people sent to do a מצוה are not harmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say: people sent to do a מצוה are not harmed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new problem: רבי אלעזר taught that people on the way to do a מצוה are protected. The boy was on a מצוה errand for his father, so how could he be killed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge does not argue that the boy was punished. It points to a different rule saying מצוות do protect a person in this world, which seems to clash with the story.

keyTerms.meaning: People sent on a מצוה mission

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
those sent to do a מצוה are not harmed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שְׁלוּחֵי מִצְוָה אֵין נִזּוֹקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from 'why was he punished' to 'why wasn't he protected by רבי אלעזר's rule.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that the boy died while doing מצוות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר's rule says a person on a מצוה mission cannot be harmed, so the event seems impossible.

steps.title: The protection is only on the way there
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי אלעזר's protection applies only on the way to the מצוה, not on the way back.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is different, because they are on their way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר's rule protects someone going to do a מצוה. The boy was harmed after he finished, on his way back down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This limits רבי אלעזר's rule to the trip there. Since the boy had already done the מצוה, the rule no longer covered him.

phrases.english: There, on their way there, it is different.
phrases.notes: The boy fell on the way back down, after he had already done the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by narrowing רבי אלעזר's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the challenging rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The protection covers the whole mission, so the boy should have been safe.
steps.terutzMaskana: The protection covers only the trip to the מצוה, and the boy fell on his return.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר also protects the return trip
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר's fuller statement: no harm either going or returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי אלעזר say: people sent to do a מצוה are not harmed, not on their way there and not on their way back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the last answer. רבי אלעזר said clearly that the protection covers both the trip there and the trip back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'going versus returning' answer no longer works, because the boy was still covered on his way down. The question returns: why was he harmed?

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
those sent to do a מצוה are not harmed,
not on their way there and not on their way back!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שְׁלוּחֵי מִצְוָה אֵינָן נִזּוֹקִין לֹא בַּהֲלִיכָתָן וְלֹא בַּחֲזִירָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 20 with a fuller version of רבי אלעזר's teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the protection is only on the way there.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר explicitly includes the return trip, so the boy should have been protected.

steps.title: A shaky ladder is clear danger, and we don't rely on miracles
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ladder was rickety, so the danger was obvious, and we do not rely on a miracle where danger is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a rickety ladder, so the danger was established. And wherever danger is established, we do not rely on a miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר's protection does not cover a place of obvious danger. The boy climbed a shaky ladder, which is a clear risk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's rule protects against ordinary, unexpected harm. Where danger is clear and set, staying safe would take a miracle, and we may not count on one. So the boy's death does not contradict רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The danger is established and obvious
We do not rely on a miracle

steps.whatToRemember: Being on a מצוה mission protects a person from ordinary harm, but not where danger is obvious. There we may not rely on a miracle.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'where danger is established we do not rely on a miracle' is a well-known principle about not putting oneself in clear danger, even while doing a מצוה.

phrases.english: It was a rickety ladder,
where the danger is established,
and anywhere the danger is established,
we do not rely on a miracle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by limiting רבי אלעזר's protection to cases without obvious danger.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case: obvious danger is outside the protection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מצוה mission protects from every kind of harm, both going and returning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The protection does not cover obvious danger like a rickety ladder, because we do not rely on miracles.

steps.title: Proof from שמואל's fear of שאול
steps.stepSummary: The rule against relying on miracles is proven from שמואל, who feared שאול would kill him even though God had sent him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And שמואל said: How can I go? שאול will hear and kill me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to prove that even someone sent by God does not rely on a miracle when danger is clear. שמואל was sent to anoint דוד, yet he feared שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל was on a mission straight from God, the strongest kind of מצוה mission. Still he worried about real danger. This shows that clear danger is not ignored even during a מצוה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יעקב's proof survives every challenge: the boy's death shows that the reward for מצוות is not paid in this world.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Samuel said: How can I go?
Saul will hear and kill me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the principle stated in step 22 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that we do not rely on a miracle where danger is established.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 16:2: שמואל, though sent by God, feared שאול would kill him.

steps.title: If אחר had read the verse correctly, he would not have sinned
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that אחר would not have sinned if he had understood the reward verse as referring to עולם הבא, the way רבי יעקב did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If אחר had explained this verse the way his grandson רבי יעקב did, he would not have sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a comment on רבי יעקב's teaching that the reward for מצוות comes in עולם הבא. He says this way of reading the verse could have saved אחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יעקב taught that 'it will be good for you' means in a world that is fully good, which is עולם הבא. Someone who expects the reward in this world can be shaken when a righteous person suffers. רב יוסף says this mistake is exactly what brought אחר down.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the Other.' This is the nickname of אֱלִישָׁע בֶּן אֲבוּיָה, a great sage who left the path of Torah.
If only / had it been that

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a wrong idea about how reward works can have real spiritual effects. Understanding that the true reward is in עולם הבא protects a person's faith.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Had Aḥer interpreted
phrases.notes: אחר is the name the גמרא uses for אלישע בן אבויה after he left the path of Torah.

phrases.english: this verse
phrases.notes: The verse is 'so that it will be good for you' (דברים 5:16).

phrases.english: like Rabbi Ya'akov, son of his daughter,
phrases.notes: 'His daughter' means אחר's daughter, so רבי יעקב was אחר's own grandson.

phrases.english: he would not have sinned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִילְמָלֵי דַּרְשֵׁיהּ אַחֵר לְהַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a comment on רבי יעקב's teaching from earlier on the daf, that reward comes in עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading the reward verse as referring to עולם הבא would have kept אחר from sinning.

steps.title: What made אחר go astray?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what event caused אחר to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what happened with אחר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what actually made אחר lose his faith. It is setting up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף only said that the right reading would have saved אחר. The גמרא now wants to know what specific event pushed him over the edge.

phrases.english: And what caused Aḥer to sin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the background behind רב יוסף's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What event caused אחר to sin.

steps.title: First version: he saw a case like the ladder story
steps.stepSummary: Some say אחר saw a son die right while doing the two מצוות that promise long life.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: he saw a case just like this one.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer. אחר saw something like the story told earlier, where a son climbed up on his father's command, sent away the mother bird, and then fell and died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כיבוד אב and שילוח הקן are the two מצוות the תורה promises long life for. Seeing someone die while doing both made אחר think there is no reward. He did not understand that the reward comes in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (one version)

phrases.english: There are those who say
he saw a case like this.
phrases.notes: 'Like this' points back to the story told earlier of the son who fell from the ladder after sending away the mother bird.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא חֲזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחר saw someone die while doing the מצוות that promise long life.

steps.title: Second version: he saw a great teacher's tongue in the dirt
steps.stepSummary: Others say אחר saw the tongue of חוצפית the speaker being dragged by a pig, and he could not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: he saw the tongue of חוצפית the speaker being dragged by a pig. He said: Should a mouth that brought out pearls lick dust?! He went out and sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, different answer to what made אחר sin. He saw a great Torah teacher's tongue treated with terrible disgrace, and it broke his faith.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the shock is not about a missing reward for one מצוה. It is seeing a great Torah teacher treated so terribly. אחר thought there could be no justice, again because he was looking for the reward in this world.

keyTerms.meaning: חוצפית the speaker, who announced the head of the yeshiva's words out loud to the crowd
Literally 'another thing.' A polite way of saying 'a pig.'

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions say אחר broke when he saw suffering that seemed unfair. רב יוסף's point is that knowing the reward comes in עולם הבא would have protected him.

phrases.english: And there are those who say
he saw the tongue of Ḥutzpit the disseminator
being dragged along by 'something else.'
phrases.notes: 'Something else' is a polite way of saying a pig.

phrases.english: He said: Shall a mouth that produced pearls
lick up dirt?!
He went out and sinned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: לִישָּׁנָא דְּחוּצְפִּית הַמְתוּרְגְּמָן חֲזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחר saw the tongue of חוצפית disgraced and lost faith in justice.

steps.title: Is reward only for doing, or also for not sinning?
steps.stepSummary: רב טובי בר רב קיסנא points out that the משנה rewards only actual doing, while a ברייתא rewards even sitting and not sinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טובי בר רב קיסנא pointed out a contradiction to רבא. We learned in the משנה: Whoever does one מצוה is treated with good. That means if he did a מצוה, yes; if he didn't, no. But a ברייתא says: Someone who sat and did not sin is given reward like one who does a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב טובי shows that two sources seem to clash about what earns a person reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording, 'whoever does,' suggests you only get reward for an action. The ברייתא gives reward even for doing nothing, just not sinning. So which is it?

keyTerms.meaning: Good is done for him (he is rewarded)
And a contradiction was raised from another source
He sat and did not commit a sin

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי רַב טוֹבִי בַּר רַב קִיסְנָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Tuvi bar Rav Kisna raised a contradiction to Rava:
We learned: Anyone who performs one מצוה
has good done for him.
If he did it, yes,
if he did not do it, no.
And they raised a contradiction:
If one sat and did not commit a sin,
he is given reward like one who performs a מצוה!

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי רַב טוֹבִי בַּר רַב קִיסְנָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the story of אחר back to the משנה's rule about reward.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's implication that reward comes only for actually doing a מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives reward even to someone who only held back from sin, so passive behavior is also rewarded.

steps.title: The ברייתא means someone who was tempted and held back
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא is talking about someone who had a chance to sin and saved himself from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: There, it means a case where a chance to sin came to him and he was saved from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the contradiction. 'Sat and did not sin' does not mean just doing nothing. It means facing a real temptation and pulling away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding back from a sin that is right in front of you takes real effort, so it counts like doing a מצוה. A person who simply never faced temptation gets no such reward. That is why it fits the משנה's rule that reward comes for something you actually did.

phrases.english: He said to him: There,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the ברייתא about the person who sat and did not sin.

phrases.english: it is a case where a chance to sin came into his hand
and he was saved from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם, כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּא דְּבַר עֲבֵירָה לְיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא rewards anyone who simply did not sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא rewards only someone who faced a real chance to sin and held back.

steps.title: The story of רבי חנינא בר פפי, who escaped temptation
steps.stepSummary: A noblewoman tried to seduce רבי חנינא בר פפי. He made himself sick to escape, she healed him, and he fled to a dangerous bathhouse where he was protected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the story of רבי חנינא בר פפי: a certain noblewoman tried to seduce him. He said a formula and covered himself with boils and sores. She did a magic act and he was healed. He ran away and hid in a bathhouse so dangerous that even two people going in together during the day would be harmed. The next day the רבנן asked him: Who protected you? He said to them: Two...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows exactly the kind of person רבא described: someone who faced a real temptation and saved himself from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא did not just sit back. He worked hard to escape, even making himself ugly and hiding in a dangerous place. This is what 'a chance to sin came to him and he was saved' looks like, and he was even protected from harm.
steps.whatToRemember: Reward for 'not sinning' is for someone who truly faced temptation and held back, like רבי חנינא בר פפי.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפֵּי
phrases.english: Like this story of Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappi:
a certain noblewoman tried to seduce him.
He said a formula
phrases.notes: Literally 'he said a thing.' He means a spoken charm to make himself sick so she would leave him alone.

phrases.english: and filled himself with boils and sores.
She did a magic act, and he was healed.
He fled and hid in a certain bathhouse
where, when people entered even two together,
even in the daytime, they would be harmed.
The next day the Sages said to him:
Who protected you?
He said to them: Two

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פַּפֵּי תְּבַעְתֵּיהּ הָהִיא מַטְרוֹנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of רבא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's explanation that the reward is for someone who faced a chance to sin and held back.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי חנינא בר פפי, who was tempted by a noblewoman and escaped.
